title: Dolly Kill Kill
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: High-schooler Iruma Ikaruga loses his ordinary life when flesh-dissolving wasps and giant doll-like monsters called dollies invade and slaughter humanity. A year later he joins a group fighting the dollies after glimpsing the girl he liked, thought dead, held captive by them.
life_message: Holding on to the people you love and refusing to give up is what keeps a person human in a collapsing world.

content.note: Reviewers call it ultraviolent, with limbs melting; AniList Gore and Body Horror, MU Massacre and Blood and Gore.
Survival horror with grotesque monsters; one reviewer calls it relentlessly bleak and cruel (ANN guide; MU Apocalypse).
Dolly scouts resemble giant pregnant schoolgirls and seem to capture only girls (ANN); no sexual content reported.
Iruma loses friends and everyone he cares about; reviewers note despair and characters who seem unhinged.
Teen fighting monsters with weapons; fantastical setting.

dominant: Survival horror; despair versus loyalty to loved ones; nihilistic atmosphere

Dignity vs honor.evidence: MU lists Revenge; Iruma answers the dollies' killing with personal combat.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Lawlessness after the invasion; survivors act on their own judgment (MU).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Driven by his best friend and the girl he liked rather than humanity at large.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Small resistance group Trial & Error with no clear hierarchy reported.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: No faith or custom guides survival; practical, weapon-based response.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Pure survival: food, safety and staying alive dominate the story.

folkways.japan: Uses the shonen survival-horror mold (ordinary student, sudden apocalypse, cute-grotesque monsters) common in Japanese web manga.

delivery.evidence: Reviewers note bleak, cruel tone and spectacle rather than any stated message (ANN guide).

personified.ideology: stubborn hope and loyalty to friends

delivery.note: The story carries mood and loyalty through events; reviewers did not find a clear message delivered.

winners_losers: Humanity largely loses; Iruma and the resistance fight on, and sympathy goes to survivors who refuse to give up on loved ones.
to_verify: Ending and whether the captured girl and friends survive not confirmed from summaries.
Two reviews cover volume 1 only; later-volume intensity unknown.
